items.title: 70399_Theodore _Red_ Saunders oral history interview
items.q: he had Jimmy Bertrand playing drums with him

ctx.x: Well, I know the name. I've never met him.

Well, he was one of the great band leaders in the early '20s, and then at the Vendome Theatre he had this great band. And I guess back there -- I guess he had about 16 or 18 or 20 pieces, and they would play an overture and he had Jimmy Bertrand playing drums with him. He had Teddy Weatherford playing piano with him one time, then later he had Earl Hines playing with him, Louis Armstrong played with him. And Darnell -- everybody, Darnell Howard, all the guys, everybody. They played with him at one time here. And…

items.title: 70399_Theodore _Red_ Saunders oral history interview
items.q: He featured all these people -- Louis Armstrong and Jimmy Bertran and Bud Scott worked there, all these different people.

ctx.x: You were talking about Erskine Tate.

Yeah, well, I talked about Erskine -- I never -- see, he was a little before my time. He started in the '20s, he was in the '20s, and he had that great band at the Vendome Theatre. And it was just a rare treat to go -- the people used to go, not for the movie, not for whatever, they went to hear that band.

And in the band, he had greats like Earl Hines and at one time, Teddy Weatherford on piano. He featured all these people -- Louis Armstrong and Jimmy Bertran and Bud Scott worked there, all these different…
Well, did he just conduct -- well, Tate just conducted then.
